title: Finance ministry outlines infrastructure spending plan
text: The finance ministry on Tuesday presented an outline of its infrastructure spending priorities for the coming financial year, allocating the largest share to road and rail projects. Officials said capital expenditure would rise moderately compared with the previous year, with an emphasis on completing projects already under way rather than announcing new ones. A ministry spokesperson said the allocation reflected a continued focus on transport connectivity in smaller cities. Economists who reviewed the outline described the figures as broadly in line with expectations. The full budget documents are scheduled to be tabled in parliament later this month, after which standing committees will review individual departmental allocations. Opposition members have indicated they will seek clarification on the pace of disbursement, noting that a portion of last year's allocation remained unspent at the close of the financial year.

title: Weather department forecasts near-normal monsoon rainfall
text: The national weather department said on Monday that rainfall during the coming monsoon season is expected to be near normal, based on current ocean temperature readings and atmospheric models. In its first long-range forecast of the year, the department placed expected rainfall within a range of five percent above or below the long-period average. Officials cautioned that the forecast covers the country as a whole and that regional variation is likely, with some districts receiving substantially more or less than the national figure. Agricultural planners said a near-normal forecast would support sowing schedules for the main summer crop, though they noted that the distribution of rainfall across the season matters more than the seasonal total. An updated forecast incorporating additional data is expected before the season begins.

title: Central bank holds benchmark lending rate unchanged
text: The central bank held its benchmark lending rate unchanged at its policy meeting on Friday, citing moderating inflation and steady growth. The monetary policy committee voted five to one in favour of holding the rate, according to minutes released after the meeting. The governor said in a statement that inflation had eased closer to the medium-term target over the previous quarter, but that the committee preferred to wait for further data before considering any adjustment. Retail inflation has declined for three consecutive months, driven largely by softer food prices. Analysts at several banks said they expected the rate to remain unchanged through the current quarter. The committee is scheduled to meet again in two months.
